note: Bci only: Banco de Chile's card pages answered with a captcha and its 'tarifas claras' page didn't answer, Santander Chile's site refused the request (403), and BancoEstado's returned no tariff, so Bci, among the largest card issuers, is the one bank whose full range could be read. Bci's tariff of charges for individuals (updated 7 May 2025, read again 30 October 2026) and its table of card interest (updated 15 November 2025), read in full: every personal Visa and Mastercard it prices (31; the Empresario and Business cards aren't written). Each card's yearly administration charge comes in two parts: a half-yearly charge in UF, waived in full when the card's purchases in Chile average more than a stated UF figure a month over the six months (10 UF on most cards, 13 on BciPlus Classic, Gold and Platinum, 40 on the AAdvantage cards and BciPlus Signature, Black and Infinite), written as spending six times that figure over the half year (the 50% discount on a lower average is a step not written, nor the waiver for holders of a Bci current-account plan, which the game doesn't check); and a monthly charge in UF for the cards the tariff names (cards it doesn't name pay between UF 0.06 and 0.10 a month, a range not written). The monthly charge isn't made in a month the card isn't used and carries no debt, which the game doesn't distinguish. Charges are made in pesos at the UF's value on the first of the month; at the Unidad de Fomento's value on 1 October 2026, 41,065.38 pesos (the tax service's table), each is written in whole pesos. A purchase abroad costs 2.5% of its amount, except on the cards the tariff exempts. A cash advance in Chile costs nothing. Interest is 9.84% to 48.96% a year on every card (the table names the Visa and Mastercard ranges together), written at the top with the bottom as the range's lowest. No minimum payment, grace period or late fee is stated.
